title: Scale document block
description: An ordered progression of values (a type scale, spacing scale, elevation scale, or similar). Each step links to a token, or (when none exists) carries a literal value, plus an optional name and usage notes. A scale is the limited set designers and engineers choose from, instead of picking arbitrary values.

scaleStep.description: One step in the scale. Maps to a `token` (if it's token-backed) or a literal `value` (if not) — never both. At least one is required. Use a value-only step when a token does not exist.

token.description: The token that supplies this step's value. MUST match a token defined elsewhere in the system. Omit if this step isn't token-backed and use `value` instead.

name.description: A short name for this step (ex: 'sm', 'lg', 'heading-1'). Represents the shorthand people use to talk about it without naming a raw value.

value.description: The resolved value (ex: '16px'), for a step that has no token. MUST be omitted when `token` is set — the token's DTCG file is the source of truth, and this document must not carry a copy that can fork from it.

description.description: Usage notes. Defines when to use this step, what it pairs with, and any limits (ex: 'The base unit; use for default padding.').

scale.description: An ordered scale (a deliberate progression that keeps design decisions consistent). Used for spacing, type, elevation, and similar graduated systems. Steps run smallest to largest; tools SHOULD keep this order.

kind.description: Identifies this block as a scale spec.

name.description: Human-readable name of the scale (ex: 'Spacing Scale', 'Type Scale', 'Elevation Levels').

description.description: What the scale is, how it was built (ex: geometric progression), and how to use it. Defines why these values are used, and when it's okay to deviate.

steps.description: The steps, smallest to largest. Tools SHOULD keep this order. When adjusting a value, consumers SHOULD move to the adjacent step.
